definition: VC Dimension is a measure of the capacity of a statistical classification model, defined as the size of the largest dataset that can be shattered by the classifier.
details: VC Dimension is a measure of the capacity of a statistical classification model, defined as the size of the largest dataset that can be shattered by the classifier. It helps in understanding the model's ability to generalize to unseen data.

explainer.lead: VC dimension measures the capacity of a statistical classification model as the size of the largest dataset it can shatter. It matters because it helps in understanding the model's ability to generalize to unseen data.

tiers.eli5: It's a score for how flexibly a classifier can separate points — the bigger the set it can split in every possible way, the higher its score.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to reason about model capacity versus generalization to unseen data. The pitfall is treating high capacity alone as predictive of good generalization.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the size of the largest dataset that can be shattered by the classifier. Limits: it is a capacity measure for classification, and its role is in understanding generalization rather than directly guaranteeing it.

explainer.example: If a classifier can shatter every labeling of some dataset of size d but not of size d+1, its VC dimension is d.
